items.question: What order do the rows come out in?
items.chose: Sorts rows by creation time ascending, with ties broken by id compared as strings, and leaves the input array unchanged.
items.instead: Keep the caller's input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: Which columns appear, in what order, and under what header text?
items.ticket: requisition list (with status and fill counts)
items.instead: Use other header labels or column order, for example snake_case field names, or add a computed open-slots column.

items.question: What does an empty requisition list produce?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and the header row with a trailing CRLF and no data rows.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or the header only without a BOM.

items.question: Which line terminator is used, and does the last row end with one?
items.chose: Ends every line, including the last, with CRLF.
items.instead: Join lines with '\n', or with CRLF and no trailing terminator.

items.question: Does the output start with a UTF-8 byte order mark?
items.instead: Emit plain CSV with no BOM and leave Excel compatibility to the download layer.

items.question: How are text fields escaped when they contain commas, quotes or line breaks?
items.chose: Wraps the field in double quotes and doubles any inner quotes (RFC 4180) when it contains a comma, quote, CR or LF.
items.instead: Quote every text field, or also neutralize leading =, +, - or @ to prevent spreadsheet formula injection.

items.question: How is a missing (null or undefined) title rendered?
items.instead: Write a placeholder such as 'Untitled' or '-', or throw.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has a status outside open, on_hold, filled or cancelled?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id and the status.
items.instead: Write the status through as-is, or skip the row.

items.question: What happens when openings or filled is negative, fractional, NaN or infinite?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id, and accepts 0 as valid for both counts.
items.instead: Clamp or round the value, skip the row, or require openings of at least 1.

items.question: What happens when filled is greater than openings?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id.
items.instead: Export the row as-is, or cap filled at openings.

items.question: What happens when createdAt is not a valid Date?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id.
items.instead: Write an empty date cell, or skip the row.

items.question: Does one bad requisition abort the whole export, and how is the date formatted?
items.chose: Validates every row before building any output, so one invalid row throws for the whole export, and formats createdAt as a full UTC ISO-8601 string with milliseconds.
items.instead: Skip invalid rows or collect the errors, and format the date as a date-only value (YYYY-MM-DD) or in the employer's local time zone.
